g.text: 0 · THE FRESH BRAIN: what is hand laid (his outline 10-25 21:50; v1 10-19)
1 · THE LINE ARRIVES: prompt > encoder > brain (10-25: never a told block between)
2 · STANDING QUESTIONS: three runs that ask before the main run runs (10-23 P3 B2; his sketch 10-28: three columns)
3 · THE MAIN RUN R1, the hallway: 61 > 3 > 62 > 3 > 63 (10-23 P3: it writes nothing but its receipt; the triggers do the rest)
4 · BORN RUN R2 for 61, THE LONG WAY: a run through the SQL-word neurons, one hit per symbol, the value neuron holding the hole (10-19 21:52; 23:03; his words 10-28: 'like 50 neurons gates')
5 · BORN RUNS R4 (62) and R6 (63), THE SHORTCUT: born > CREATE jumps to the formula row; write run writes the value; substitution run plugs it in; build (his words 10-28)

6 · SOURCE RUNS R3 (61), R5 (62), R7 (63): the newborn's first memory is its definition, pulled from every source and compared (10-23 P5-9; 10-25 msg 51). Each source run has its own sheet; one answer goes back to R1.
7 · THE THREE NEWBORNS AFTER THE LINE: DNA, definition node with its rows and relationships, memory nodes per ending shard
8 · INSPECTION RUN: a row that decides which row to hit (10-23 P2 B1; P3 B1). On this line no gate has two rows for one arrival, so it is not called.
9 · THE END OF R1 and the TIMELINE: no remainder > memory > timeline > stop (10-26 03:50)
10 · OUTPUT: a separate mechanism from the same memory table (10-26 03:50): when no declared cell of R1 is empty
11 · THE SIXTH and THE GUESSING BRAIN
12 · WHAT HIS WORDS LEAVE OPEN (his calls, not filled)
one HIT of a gate in a run (the neuron drawn where it is hit)
DEFINITION NODE (born with the neuron; its first memory)
MEMORY NODE on the shard that ended a run (the data sheet inside)

g.title: The run moves to the remainder's head: before and after; the key is the remainder (§12 law 13). Blue thick wire.
A DNA row excites a run: one, none or many (10-26 05:12). It writes nothing itself; it excites a write, copy or cut run (10-26 03:59). Orange dashed.
A side run whose answer comes back to this run's cell (his sketch: 'call gate 9,8,7' loops back). Green dotted.
A run that goes off on its own (his sketch: 'spawn gate 5,4,3' leaves). Purple dashed.

Skip the long run: go straight to the formula neuron, plug the value in (10-18 J: 'plug them in and you go to that gate'; his words 10-28: 'skip the long run and use the formula neuron'). Black thick.
Mother routes and traverses, decides nothing, works no data (10-23 P2). Red.
10-26 03:50: each return from the graph, from source or from another brain fills its spot on the table. Teal dotted.
A read run over memory, timeline or definition nodes (standing questions, inspection). Grey dotted.
A path his words describe that this line does not take.
What his words leave to him. Listed in the last lane; not filled in.

g.title: His outline 10-25 21:50: build the user input mailbox to the encoder. Populated-driven, never a timer (10-22 rev17).
His outline: the secondary input mailbox to the encoder from the mother. SQL answers and source answers come back this way (10-24 msg 36).
His outline: the third input mailbox to the encoder from the sixth.db.

His outline: the mailbox output from the brain to the mother and from the brain to the user. Gate 60 is the port neuron the run hits to leave (10-23 msg 1: output to sources is a dna row and trigger to port).

10-23 P2: the mother is just a router and a traverser. That's it... takes the output and traverses it to the sources, or to another brain, or to its own sql... picks up the outputs of whatever it traversed to and brings it back. She works no data. The name is probably wrong.

g.text: THE NEURON PROMPT (the brain's own sql prompt)

g.title: A neuron is its own table; its name is its gate (10-19 21:14). Rows are its DNA: his sketch 10-28 gives the columns shard id | before | trigger | call | spawn. The run arrives from before, goes on to trigger, calls side runs that return, spawns runs that leave.
In a run column every box is one hit of a gate, drawn where the run hits it, as in his sketch (gate 5,6,7 drawn down the column). The row shown is the shard this run hit or wrote.
A gate that did not exist when the line arrived: born by the born run (10-20 01:22; 10-19 23:40).

10-19 23:40: a new gate, new dna table and new definition node are born at the same time. 10-23 P2: the first birth memory is the definition, pulled from the sources. Its rows: one per source line, and the relationships built from the definition table (10-23 P5-9).

10-23 P2 B2: each DNA shard that ends a run will have a memory table for that shard. 10-26 03:50: the data sheet just lives in a cell in the memory row. His v4 brain.db 10-27: run_memory(run, input, source) + run_sheet(run, cell, state, value). A neuron with several shards that end runs has several memory nodes (his words 10-28).
10-16 06:40: the timeline only gets the receipt number as a pointer, and a couple key words. 10-26 03:50: memory triggers timeline and it just stops because timeline is only a memory table.
The run moves to the remainder's head: before and after; the key is the remainder (§12 law 13). Blue thick wire.
A DNA row excites a run: one, none or many (10-26 05:12). It writes nothing itself; it excites a write, copy or cut run (10-26 03:59). Orange dashed.
A side run whose answer comes back to this run's cell (his sketch: 'call gate 9,8,7' loops back). Green dotted.
A run that goes off on its own (his sketch: 'spawn gate 5,4,3' leaves). Purple dashed.

Skip the long run: go straight to the formula neuron, plug the value in (10-18 J: 'plug them in and you go to that gate'; his words 10-28: 'skip the long run and use the formula neuron'). Black thick.
Mother routes and traverses, decides nothing, works no data (10-23 P2). Red.
10-26 03:50: each return from the graph, from source or from another brain fills its spot on the table. Teal dotted.
A read run over memory, timeline or definition nodes (standing questions, inspection). Grey dotted.

10-26 03:50: 'its a straight database conversion table with x,y,z gates in a sequential order, new word new gate #'. 10-25: 'there are no words in the graph... the encoder encodes to the brain'. Lands in the user input mailbox (his outline 10-25 21:50).

A symbol with no gate gets the next number; nothing else is figured here (10-26 03:50; 10-23 P2: the encoder never guesses a word or does work). Who is speaking is part of the input: user, heard (10-26 03:50; §2.1).

The main run's input row. The clock neuron (47) is hit on every run and its reading goes into the run's meta (10-26 03:50). The remainder is the rest of the line as gate numbers; its head is the key at every gate (10-23 P3).
The path of gates and shards the run hit: a pointer to the run, never the run again (10-23 P2). [open] whether the receipt is written by the hop's physics or by a write run (audit 10-25 row 5).

A row per run that ended, in the order the drawing says they happen. 't' is the clock neuron's reading. The pointer is the run's memory node; the key words are a couple of gates. The born runs of the symbols inside the definitions (the cascade) add their own rows, not listed.

CREATE TABLE run_memory (run INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, input TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE run_sheet (run REFERENCES run_memory(run), cell INTEGER, state INTEGER DEFAULT 0 CHECK(state IN (0,1)), value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(run,cell)). His own typing, 10-27 01:17. The sheet lives inside the memory row (10-26 03:50). One such node per shard that ends a run (10-23 P2 B2).

CREATE TABLE definition (id, neuron, source, entry, sense, class, text, example, origin, first_use, synonyms, antonyms, times, first_at, last_at, ended_at). His own typing. Born with the neuron (10-19 23:40); first memory (10-23 P2); truth shift keeps the old row (10-23 P4: ended_at). Relationships are built from this table and self-populate (10-23 P5-9; P4: opposite, kind of, part, has, plural, past, present, is, same spelling, derived from, used in, prefix, suffix, modifier, mood, rhyming).

SQ1 'Do I know anything about this?' (10-23 P3 B2). A read run over the gates of the input and their definition nodes. Fresh brain: 61, 62, 63 have no gate. Answer 0. The build neuron: ’the last build word was the build neuron... routing information for the mother... build neuron = routing to sql prompt’ (10-26 03:50). Its DNA row, picked by before (10 ;) and remainder (none), is a build row ’because of how the before and remainder are set’, not by counting BUILDs. No remainder: this shard ends R2, so it carries R2’s memory node. The build neuron ends every born run, so it has one memory node per born run (his words 10-28).

10-19 23:03: the statement ’as the product of the run’. 10-24 msg 36: the run data sheet ’then produces the exact code that sql needs to run as output the same way that it forms human sentences... that output is given to the mother to route to the sql prompt’.

The answer comes back through the mother > encoder mailbox as secondary input and fills R2’s cell reply (10-24 msg 36; 10-26 03:50). An error is not an end: ’the brain would problem solve’ (10-27 03:52).

R2’s memory row on the shard that ended it, with its data sheet inside (10-26 03:50; his v4 run_sheet). Cells declared by the triggers that tripped: value (write run), text and reply (build), exists (read run), formula (decide run), backpop (write run).
One row per run that ends: the clock reading, the receipt pointer, a couple of key words (10-16 06:40).

[reading] ’the first time it works, and is correct’ (his words 10-28): ok says it ran; correct is read back: the read run asks the prompt (.schema of 61) through mother and the answer fills cell exists = 1. Which check counts as ’correct’ is his call.

His words 10-28: ’the first time it works, and is correct, it triggers a decide formula run that decides what the formula is, then writes it in that runs data sheet’. The decide formula run reads R2’s receipt, marks the hole (the value neuron’s shard 18.s117), and writes the formula into R2’s sheet cell formula: the receipt with the hole. The formula is a pointer to the run, never text (10-23 08:47: ’the row holds pointers to the run through the neurons that makes that’).

The formula neuron for CREATE TABLE value ( shard INTEGER , before INTEGER , trigger INTEGER , call INTEGER , spawn INTEGER ) (his words 10-28). Its new row s253: arrived from 4 (CREATE arriving from born), goes on to 40 (build); calls the write run (43) and the substitution run (54). The row’s trigger points at R2’s sheet cell formula (the receipt with the hole). [open] one formula neuron with a row per formula, as drawn, or one neuron per formula (10-23 08:47 ’a pointer to the shortcut neuron formula’).

His words 10-28: ’through back population the triggers or calls or jumps or hops from a run create table (value) would have to show the substitution run and the write run writing the value... so that you can then skip the long run and use the formula neuron’. The write run (43) updates the first shard of the long run (CREATE arriving from born) with a jump to the formula row. 10-23 P5-9: back population is the application of a newly understood process to the other things it fits.
The same born neuron, a new shard for this run: arrived from 62, goes on to 4 (CREATE); spawns the ask run (51) for the newborn's sources.

The same shard 4.s112 the long run wrote, now carrying the jump laid by back population: the long run is skipped. 10-08: ’if I know where I am standing I can hop to any point in my brain in one step... all the work was done at learning, not at runtime’.
The formula row laid after R2. Calls the write run and the substitution run; goes on to build.
The write run writes the value variable, 62, into R4's sheet cell value (his words 10-28: 'the formula shortcut is just to the data sheet writing the value varible').

The substitution run: ’substitution run grabbing that value and plugging it into the run data sheet so a new memory node can be made or a new neuron can be made’ (his words 10-28). Its call: the copy run (44) copies the formula (R2’s sheet cell formula, the receipt with the hole) into this run’s sheet; then the hole is filled with cell value = 62. ’the trigger of the substitution run copying into the substitution run’ (10-28).
Copies R2.sheet.formula into R4's sheet cell text (the receipt with the hole).
The build neuron again, a new shard for R4: it ends the run, so it carries another memory node. The build neuron now holds memory nodes for R2, R4, ... one per born run.
A separate memory node on a separate ending shard of the same neuron 40, with its own sheet inside (his words 10-28).
The same born neuron, a new shard for this run: arrived from 63, goes on to 4 (CREATE); spawns the ask run (51) for the newborn's sources.

The same shard 4.s112 the long run wrote, now carrying the jump laid by back population: the long run is skipped. 10-08: ’if I know where I am standing I can hop to any point in my brain in one step... all the work was done at learning, not at runtime’.
The formula row laid after R2. Calls the write run and the substitution run; goes on to build.
The write run writes the value variable, 63, into R6's sheet cell value (his words 10-28: 'the formula shortcut is just to the data sheet writing the value varible').

The substitution run: ’substitution run grabbing that value and plugging it into the run data sheet so a new memory node can be made or a new neuron can be made’ (his words 10-28). Its call: the copy run (44) copies the formula (R2’s sheet cell formula, the receipt with the hole) into this run’s sheet; then the hole is filled with cell value = 63. ’the trigger of the substitution run copying into the substitution run’ (10-28).
Copies R2.sheet.formula into R6's sheet cell text (the receipt with the hole).
The build neuron again, a new shard for R6: it ends the run, so it carries another memory node. The build neuron now holds memory nodes for R2, R6, ... one per born run.
A separate memory node on a separate ending shard of the same neuron 40, with its own sheet inside (his words 10-28).

The ask run, spawned by the born run. Declares its own sheet: one cell per source (wn, gcide, mw, mwt, moby, map, sqldoc) and compile; declares on R1’s sheet the cell def.61. Assembles the ask from the encoder’s label of the newborn and goes on to 60 (out): the brain > mother mailbox. The run names the sources; mother carries the ask to each one’s inbox and decides nothing (10-23 P2; 10-23 01:28 asking the sources is the brain’s decide run).

The source run's own sheet: a cell per source, filled by each return; when no declared cell is empty the compile runs (10-26 03:50). Counts are the real lines in the archived slice (tries/11 sat172.json).

The run ends at its last symbol: its memory node sits there; the definition node row for 61 points at this receipt. The inspection run: 1. reads the main run’s input row: the symbols after this gate and before it (10-20 00:31: ’triggers will later look at the run if we need them to look at other parts of the run’); 2. reads their definition nodes: class, tense, perspective; 3. reads the run’s sheet: speaker, what is known; 4. fills its own small sheet; its answer is the shard to hit; 5. returns to the gate, which hits THAT shard (10-23 P3 B1: ’run a DNA row that actually decides what DNA row that actually needs to get hit in that gate’). 10-23 P2 B2: ’it might be more efficient if the DNA row has that... so that the run table becomes more precise’ [open: an extra column on the row].
